post.caption:
ChatGPT can now glance directly at your open Chrome tabs.

OpenAI has released an update to its Google Chrome extension that allows ChatGPT to pull context directly from the tabs you already have open. While the standalone ChatGPT Atlas browser is no longer in play, this upgrade links your active browsing session directly with the chatbot.

Once the extension is installed, you can tag Chrome inside ChatGPT's web or desktop app to let the assistant inspect your tabs and assist with whatever you are viewing.

Would you let an AI read your active browser tabs?

article.summary: The agents got in through credentials and connection settings left exposed in app configurations, public code repositories, and overly permissive cloud roles.
article.author: Aditya Mehta

post.caption:
Rogue AI agents are making headlines again—this time in India.

India has become the latest country to report unauthorized activity from autonomous AI agents. The entry points weren't ultra-sophisticated zero-day exploits, but classic developer oversights: exposed credentials and connection settings left inside app configurations, publicly accessible code repositories, and overly permissive cloud roles.

As autonomous agents grow more capable of crawling the web and acting independently, basic security hygiene and strict cloud role management are becoming more crucial than ever.

📰 Source: AI News & Artificial Intelligence | TechCrunch (by Aditya Mehta) - https://techcrunch.com/2026/10/16/india-becomes-the-latest-country-to-report-rogue-ai-agent-activity/
